clue.text: Short ballad a mystery writer pens is revelation

indicators.note: to pen is to enclose, so the writer's name wraps around the shortened song

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe, pioneer of the detective story

indicators.note: short means the song loses its final letter

parts.note: a calypso is a Caribbean ballad

explanation.surface: A clipped song which a crime novelist writes turns out to reveal all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' drops the last letter of the song and 'pens' puts it inside Poe; 'revelation' also hints at the Bible's final book.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocalypse is the biblical Book of Revelation, and by extension any great disclosure.

clue.text: Stuff brought to junction in vehicle

parts.note: a T-junction, abbreviated to its letter
to ram is to stuff or cram

explanation.surface: Goods hauled to a road junction in a lorry.
explanation.walkthrough: The charade puts the junction letter first although the clue names it second; 'brought to' joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A tram is a passenger vehicle running on rails in the street.

clue.text: Brilliant Christmas tree entertains domestic goddess

indicators.note: to entertain is to host, so the tree holds the goddess within it

parts.note: a fir is the usual Christmas tree
Vesta was the Roman goddess of the hearth and home

explanation.surface: A dazzling Christmas tree plays host to a fine home cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Domestic goddess' suggests a celebrity cook, but here it is the Roman deity VESTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-star hotel or performance is top-rated, hence excellent.

clue.text: Vergers from Treguier love month in Paris?

indicators.note: the edges or verges of the word, its first and last letters

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O
Jan is the short form of January

explanation.surface: Church officials from a Breton town love a month in the French capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vergers' appears to be a misprint for 'verges', the outer letters TR of Treguier. 'Paris?' is not the city but the prince of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris, who abducted Helen, was a prince of Troy, so a citizen of that city; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Celebratory communication shows wit

definitions.meaning: a birthday or anniversary greeting sent through the post
an amusing, eccentric person, a joker

explanation.definitionFit: A greetings card marks celebrations, and calling someone a card means they are a joker.

clue.text: Notice one in cathedral gains control

parts.note: an ad is a notice or advertisement

indicators.note: in places the numeral inside the church

parts.note: a minster is a large church, such as York Minster
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: An advertisement placed in a cathedral wins power.
explanation.definitionFit: To administer is to manage, run or have charge of something.

clue.text: Uncouth agent breaks up on faulty line

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the preceding part
something faulty is broken, so these letters are reordered
breaking something up scatters its parts, so these letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A spy falls apart over a bad phone connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faulty' and 'breaks up' each shuffle their own word; in an across answer 'on' means coming after, so the line's letters lead.
explanation.definitionFit: Inelegant behaviour lacks grace and refinement, so is crude or unpolished.

clue.text: HM enters church society as goddess

indicators.note: entering means going inside the church abbreviation

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England
Her Majesty, Elizabeth Regina, abbreviated ER

explanation.surface: The Queen walks into a church club, playing a deity.
explanation.definitionFit: Ceres was the Roman goddess of agriculture and grain.

clue.text: Gas pipe redirected supplies Irishwoman

indicators.note: sent the opposite way, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen, a gas
a main is a principal pipe for water or gas

explanation.surface: A rerouted gas pipe supplies a woman from Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' turns HMAIN backwards. 'Gas pipe' reads as one item but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Niamh is a common Irish girl's name, from the goddess of Irish legend.

clue.text: Country ale knocked back after French arrive at university

indicators.note: after puts the reversed drink behind the French verb and the college letter

parts.note: venez is French for come, arrive

indicators.note: drinking it down, but here turning the word backwards

explanation.surface: Beer drunk quickly once the French students reach campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked back' suggests downing a pint but means reading the drink backwards; 'after' places it last.
explanation.definitionFit: Venezuela is a nation on the north coast of South America.

clue.text: Publisher cuts prison story that's refreshingly tasty

parts.note: can is slang for prison

indicators.note: cutting into something means splitting it, so the publisher goes inside

parts.note: a tale is a story
OUP is Oxford University Press

explanation.surface: A publishing house edits a prison memoir that turns out to be a delight.
explanation.definitionFit: A melon is a cool, juicy fruit, so a refreshing thing to eat, described here cryptically.

clue.text: Beat off Leonidas? Here's metal pole

indicators.note: off means the beating word is removed

parts.note: Leonidas was the king of Sparta at Thermopylae, an example of a Spartan
to tan someone is to beat them

explanation.surface: Fight off the Spartan king? Here is an iron rod.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beat off' looks like repelling an attacker, but it means deleting TAN from SPARTAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar is a stout pole, such as a mast or boom on a ship, now often made of metal.

clue.text: One-dimensional words disheartened Antenor

parts.note: an actor's line is the words spoken

indicators.note: losing its heart means only the outside letters remain

explanation.surface: Flat lines delivered by a dejected Trojan elder.
explanation.walkthrough: Antenor was a Trojan counsellor in Homer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something linear extends along a line, having length only.

clue.text: Gloria misused companion boss in limited company

indicators.note: used wrongly, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: CH stands for Companion of Honour, a British order

explanation.surface: Gloria abused her colleague, the head of a small firm.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of a small ruling group, so a leader among few.

clue.text: Ordinary wife's success, in part

indicators.note: in part says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A spouse's triumph, partly.
explanation.walkthrough: Ordinary is a heraldic term: one of the simple bold charges on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: A fess is a horizontal band across a shield, one of the heraldic ordinaries.

clue.text: Send battered fish minus tail for broadcaster

indicators.note: beaten about, so these letters are rearranged
minus tail means the fish loses its last letter

parts.note: a herring is a fish

explanation.surface: Send out battered fish without its tail for the presenter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'battered' makes NEDS from SEND; Ned Sherrin was a British broadcaster and satirist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ned Sherrin presented radio and television programmes for decades, such as Loose Ends.

clue.text: Liking forces engaged initially in battle

indicators.note: in places the troops inside the battle word

parts.note: an action is a battle or engagement
F is force, so FF is its plural, as in pp for pages

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Soldiers committed early in combat find they like it.
explanation.walkthrough: Doubling a letter for a plural is a convention, as pp for pages; the troops and the first letter go just after the opening A of the battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Affection is fondness, a warm liking for someone.

clue.text: Bowled in stint with English side facing

indicators.note: in places the cricket letter inside the stint

parts.note: a bowler's spell or stint is measured in overs
B is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for bowled

explanation.surface: Taken out during a spell of play, with an English team in opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a bowler bowls in overs of six balls.
explanation.definitionFit: The obverse of a coin is its main face, the side turned towards the viewer.

clue.text: Good to be in Harley Street, finally treated for condition

indicators.note: treated means processed, so these letters are rearranged
finally takes the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Going to Harley Street at last to be cured of an ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: Harley Street in London is famous for private doctors, which supports the medical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethargy is a state of sluggishness and lack of energy, a physical condition.

clue.text: A part Tudor women played in literotica?

indicators.note: played means acted out in a new way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A role Tudor ladies took in racy fiction?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literotica' blends literature and erotica, so it is an example of a word built from two others.
explanation.definitionFit: A blend coined from parts of two words, as literotica is, is called this.

clue.text: Accommodation provided after former partner gives amount

indicators.note: after places the camping word behind the former partner

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
a tent provides accommodation when camping

explanation.surface: Lodging supplied after a divorce gives a sum.
explanation.definitionFit: Extent means size or scope, the amount of something.

clue.text: Bottom drawer opening for theoretical philosopher

indicators.note: opening for takes the first letter of the word

parts.note: Jean-Jacques Rousseau, the Genevan philosopher

explanation.surface: The lowest drawer is the starting point for an abstract thinker.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottom drawer is British for the clothes and linen a woman saves for her marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is a bride's collection of clothes and household linen, the British bottom drawer.

clue.text: Answer arrived about extremely discursive intellectual world

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the arrival word goes round the edges

parts.note: came means arrived

indicators.note: the extremes of the word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An answer arrives concerning a very rambling academic world.
explanation.definitionFit: Academe is the academic community, the world of scholarship.

clue.text: Unending as fastest stretch on Autobahn, say

definitions.text: as fastest stretch on Autobahn, say
definitions.meaning: stretches of German motorway with no speed restriction

explanation.definitionFit: Something without bounds is unending, and parts of the Autobahn have no speed cap.

clue.text: Spiny animal takes look round posh home

indicators.note: round means the look word surrounds the posh letter

parts.note: to search is to look
U means upper class, posh
in means at home

explanation.surface: A prickly creature looks round a grand house.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea urchin is a marine echinoderm covered in spines.

clue.text: Excited at all times in school?

indicators.note: in places the always word inside the school

parts.note: a school is a group of fish, so fish are what make one
ever means always

explanation.surface: Agitated all the time at school?
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' suggests lessons, but it is a shoal of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish means agitated and overexcited, as if burning with fever.

clue.text: See the writer's Swift changing name for Lilliput's leader

parts.note: the writer is I, so the writer's is I'm, I am

indicators.note: changing one letter for another swaps the leader for the name letter

parts.note: agile means swift

indicators.note: the first letter of the word it picks from

parts.note: the first letter of Lilliput

explanation.surface: Picture the author Swift altering a name for the ruler of Lilliput.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swift' looks like Jonathan Swift, author of Gulliver's Travels, but means AGILE; 'changing' swaps its L for N.
explanation.definitionFit: To imagine is to see something in the mind's eye.

clue.text: Salesman splitting capital rises to become top man

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards
splitting means the salesman goes inside the city

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a rep is a sales representative

explanation.surface: A salesman parts the capital and rises to the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'splitting' puts the salesman inside the city, then 'rises' reads the whole result upwards, as fits a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An emperor is the supreme ruler of an empire, the topmost man.

clue.text: Stone cut to set gold coin

indicators.note: a ring setting holds a gem, so the cut stone holds the gold
cut means the stone loses its last letter

parts.note: flint is a hard stone
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: A gem cut to mount in gold for a coin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims FLINT to FLIN. The florin was an old British two-shilling coin.
explanation.definitionFit: The florin was a British coin worth two shillings, and the name of old gold coins.
